A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VD-RAG poisoning work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and generation attack results on two ViDoRe datasets, together with perturbation experiments and embedding analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original universal and targeted attack results, baseline comparisons, ablations, defense experiments and transfer/generalization evaluations, including in its appendices.

M1.justification: v1 proposes a universal attack. v2 adds targeted losses that distinguish positive and negative queries and preserve ground-truth answers for negative queries. It also evaluates joint multi-model optimization and adaptive attacks incorporating judge losses, which v1 left for future work.

E1.justification: The same two ViDoRe datasets remain. Evaluation expands from universal denial-of-service to selective misinformation targeting individual queries, query groups sharing an answer, and queries requiring different malicious answers. Paraphrased-query and defended-pipeline scenarios are also added.

E2.justification: v1 has no competing attack baseline. v2 introduces GPT-4o-generated adversarial images as a direct comparator across the universal attack and all three targeted settings (Tables 1 and 3-5), adding comparative evidence throughout the principal evaluations.

E3.justification: The evaluated retrievers replace Jina-CLIP-v2 with GME-Qwen2-VL-2B. v2 adds top-5 retrieval and adaptive-training protocols, ground-truth and negative-query metrics, and judge/paraphrasing procedures. The default PGD budget and 80/20 query split remain unchanged; ASR-G-Soft largely becomes SIM-G-ADV-POS.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's perturbation sensitivity and embedding analyses, v2 adds ColPali similarity-loss/context ablations, three defense evaluations with adaptive attacks, multi-model generalization studies and detailed transferability analyses. The perturbation sweep and embedding visualizations are also revised (Table 2, Sections 6-8 and Appendices C-F).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The expanded results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline, targeted, defense and generalization outcomes. Table 3 reports ASR-R@1 of 1 and FPR-R@1 of 0 across all six proposed single-query configurations. Universal results are also revised alongside the attack formulation: ColPali-SmolVLM on ViDoRe-V1-AI has ASR-G-Hard 0.900 in v1 Table 1 and 0.050 in v2 Table 1.

T1.justification: v2 extends the mathematical definitions with positive/negative query sets and revised retrieval and generation objectives (Equations 2-3). Appendix E additionally defines a symmetrized, normalized late-interaction quantity for UMAP. These are localized formal extensions without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The core contribution expands from universal denial-of-service to both denial-of-service and selective misinformation. v2 adds claims that common defenses can be bypassed and explicitly limits ColPali/GME robustness to universal attacks, while asserting vulnerability to targeted attacks.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the earlier ColPali robustness interpretation by attack type and attributes part of that robustness to the similarity loss. It adds interpretations of adaptive-defense failures and replaces v1's deferred-defense discussion with limitations concerning majority-vote detection, latency/benign-performance tradeoffs and compute constraints (Appendix H).

D1.justification: v1 documents PGD settings and model/data sources. v2 additionally supplies H100 GPU/VRAM details, a repository reference for code, configurations and results, attacker-data access and target-query selection details, full judge prompts in Appendix G, and UMAP construction details in Appendix E.

R1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated Related Work section substantially expanding coverage of multimodal applications, retrieval-only pixel poisoning, attack designs and RAG defenses. Discussion of Zhuang et al., RobustRAG and TrustRAG sharpens its positioning around joint retrieval-and-generation attacks.

P1.justification: The abstract, attack exposition and results narrative are substantially rewritten and reorganized. v2 introduces dedicated related-work, universal-attack, targeted-attack and defense sections, while moving perturbation, limitations and ethics discussions into an expanded appendix structure.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. The combined results table is split and expanded with additional metrics and baseline blocks; numerous comparison tables are added. UMAP displays replace t-SNE plots, and the perturbation figure becomes a six-panel display.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important evaluation gaps in v1 through an explicit attack baseline, targeted tests of otherwise robust retrievers, and defense/adaptive-attack experiments that v1 deferred. Hardware, code and prompt disclosures substantially improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, notably v2's broad generation-success prose despite the ColPali-SmolVLM ASR-G-Hard of 0.050 in Table 1.
